title: Helicity decoupling ultrastrong Rabi splitting from quantum vacuum dressing
authors: Ayoub El-Amrani, Nasir Boubekraoui, Zakaria Mzaouali, Houssam Sabri, Herschel Rabitz, Abdelouahed El Fatimy, Dukhyung Lee
abstract: Polaritons and quantum vacuum dressing are usually regarded as intertwined consequences of ultrastrong light-matter coupling. Here we show that they can be controlled independently through helicity. We consider cyclotron resonance coupled to a chiral cavity supporting a single circular mode. When the helicity of the cavity field matches the cyclotron motion, energy is exchanged resonantly between light and matter, producing a large Rabi splitting and conventional polaritons, while the ground state remains the bare vacuum. Reversing the magnetic field reverses the cyclotron motion without changing the cavity. The same mode then couples through anomalous processes that create and annihilate light and matter excitations in pairs: the conventional polaritonic anticrossing disappears, while the ground state acquires squeezing and virtual excitations. These two regimes show that spectral hybridization and quantum vacuum dressing are distinct manifestations of ultrastrong coupling, and that a large Rabi splitting alone does not imply a dressed quantum vacuum. Helicity therefore provides a route to controlling polariton formation and quantum correlations as distinct resources in cavity quantum materials.
summary: The authors show that in systems with ultrastrong light-matter coupling, the formation of polaritons and the dressing of the quantum vacuum are not equivalent. By utilizing helicity control in a chiral cavity coupled to a 2DEG, they can independently access these two regimes, proving that a large Rabi splitting alone does not guarantee a dressed vacuum state.
main_problem: To demonstrate that polariton formation (spectral hybridization) and quantum vacuum dressing are distinct physical phenomena arising from ultrastrong light-matter coupling.
main_result: By controlling the helicity of the cavity field relative to the cyclotron motion, the system can be tuned to exhibit either conventional polariton anticrossings or vacuum dressing effects, proving the two are distinct.
method: Theoretical modeling using Hamiltonian approaches and advanced numerical techniques like the Transfer Matrix Method (TMM) and full-wave finite-element simulations.
model_or_system: The system involves cyclotron resonance coupled to a chiral cavity supporting a single circular mode, realized in a 2DEG coupled to a photonic crystal cavity.
key_observables: Rabi splitting, polaritonic anticrossing, ground state squeezing, virtual excitation populations, and polarization-resolved magnetotransmission spectra.
important_parameters: Helicity ($\chi$), magnetic field direction ($B$), cyclotron frequency ($\omega_c$), and coupling strength ($g$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on a single-mode approximation for the cavity and assumes the ability to fix the cavity helicity while reversing the magnetic field on the 2DEG.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the spectral reorganization, showing a clear avoided crossing when the cavity and cyclotron motion co-rotate ($B<0$), and the disappearance of this crossing with the acquisition of vacuum correlations when they counter-rotate ($B>0$).
paper_structure: The paper establishes the physical setup using chiral cavities, develops the Hamiltonian based on helicity control, and then analyzes two distinct regimes ($B<0$ vs $B>0$) to spectroscopically and correlationally separate the effects of hybridization from vacuum dressing.
why_interesting: This work provides a clean, experimentally addressable platform (chiral cavities) to decouple two closely related, yet distinct, quantum phenomena (polaritons vs. vacuum correlations) in the regime of ultrastrong coupling, which is highly relevant to cavity QED.

Figure 2: Helicity reorganizes the ultrastrong-coupling spectrum. a, single helicity chiral cavity. For B < 0, the cavity field and cyclotron motion rotate in the same sense and form upper and lower polaritons. For B > 0, field reversal reverses the cyclotron motion but not the cavity mode, and the conventional avoided crossing disappears. b, Non-chiral cavity supporting both RCP (χ = −1) and LCP (χ = +1) modes, calculated with the same coupling strength g. For either magnetic field direction, one circular mode participates in resonant polariton formation while the other provides the anomalous interaction channel.

Figure 2 makes the role of the photonic environment explicit. In the chiral cavity (Fig. 2a), field reversal changes the type of interaction experienced by the same cavity mode. The resulting eigenfrequencies closely follow the magnetotransmission of Fig. 1: the polaritonic branches appear only when the cavity field and cyclotron motion have the same handedness, whereas the opposite field direction retains the shifted cavity-like branch without a conventional anticrossing.
